primitives.name: Player Interaction Graph
primitives.verbatim_quote: In our approach, each event in a soccer match is represented as a graph where nodes correspond to players and edges denote interactions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V': 'set of players (nodes)', 'E': 'set of player interactions (edges)', 't': 'temporal index of event'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are modeled as static nodes; interactions occur only between connected players.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When no interactions occur, E = ∅, rendering graph trivial.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE state transition graph where V represents agent states and E represents valid transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Node degree distribution and edge density over time.

primitives.name: Threat Change Attribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our model is trained to predict the expected threat (xT) changes for each event, effectively attributing these changes to the contributing players based on their interactions in the previous events.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ΔxT': 'change in expected threat (dimensionless)', 'p_i': "player i's contribution weight", 'k': 'number of past events considered'}
primitives.assumptions: Threat change ΔxT is linearly dependent on prior player interactions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When k → 0, no temporal context exists, leading to underfitting.

layer2.mapping: Derives from GNN output kernel to compute marginal contribution of each player to global threat dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual threat changes.

primitives.name: Centrality-Based Valuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: We combine metrics such as degree centrality with the output of the trained GNN model to assign xT changes as credits to players more accurately.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_{deg}(v)': 'degree centrality of node v', 'GNN(v)': 'GNN output for player v', 'W_{total}': 'weighted sum of contributions'}
primitives.assumptions: Higher centrality implies greater influence on game flow.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In symmetric teams, centrality may not distinguish high-value players.

layer2.mapping: Combines topological measure (degree) with learned GNN weights to produce composite player score.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation coefficient between centrality and observed xT credit.

This structure enables GNNs to process sequential events while preserving spatial relationships. The model's objective is to attribute changes in expected threat (xT) to individual players. This dual approach addresses limitations in traditional metrics that favor goal-scoring players. The failure mode arises when temporal dependencies are insufficiently captured or when network topology becomes too sparse, reducing predictive fidelity.
